correctness.rationale: For periodic mass |E|=mn and exactly one firing per vertex, a vertex scheduled at time tau(v) has x(v)>=deg(v)-number of neighbors fired earlier. Summing inequalities over v, any simultaneously-firing edge would force mass>|E|, impossible; equality gives x(v)=number of neighbors firing later. With no empty round and all firing rounds independent, every round lies within one shore and adjacent cyclic rounds must alternate, since a later vertex from the same shore could already fire earlier. Thus least period must be 2k with 1<=k<=min(m,n). Conversely arbitrary two ordered partitions into k nonempty blocks with one of two starting shores produce a unique valid initial chip vector, and the exact one-fire property prevents shorter period. Count gives 2(k!)^2 S(m,k)S(n,k) and divide by 2k for temporal orbits. Independently enumerated *every* nonnegative critical-mass configuration for K_(1,1), K_(1,3), K_(2,2), K_(2,3), K_(3,3) via distinct deterministic state-iteration code, matching counts (2); (2); (2,8); (2,24); (2,72,72) respectively. General formula established by the combinatorial bijection, not these finite checks.
